post.summary: Updates the subscription of Firebox Templates on a Firebox.
post.description: Subscribes, unsubscribes, or changes the order of Firebox templates on a Firebox. Specify only the template IDs in the *templates* parameter that you want the Firebox to subscribe to. The Firebox is unsubscribed from templates that you do not include. An empty *templates* array unsubscribes the Firebox from all templates. Specify template IDs in the order of priority to apply on the Firebox.

reorder.summary: Change the order of subscribed Firebox templates.

200.description: Successfully updated the subscription status of a template on a Firebox.

get.summary: Retrieves a list of devices or details of a specific device for a WatchGuard Cloud account.
get.description: Retrieves a list of Fireboxes, FireClusters, and Access Points for the specified WatchGuard Cloud account. You can specify a type of device in the *device_type* parameter, to filter the list with Fireboxes and FireClusters (FB) or Access Points (AP) details. To get details of a specific device, specify the device ID in the *device* parameter. For Service Provider accounts, set *include_hierarchy* to true to include devices from Subscriber accounts. Subscriber accounts ignore this parameter. The *device* and *include_hierarchy* parameters are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: device_type
parameters.description: Specifies the type of device to get in the response. Allowed values are `ALL` (Fireboxes, FireClusters, and Access Points), `FB` (Fireboxes and FireClusters only), `AP` (Access Points only). If not specified, all device types are returned. The *device* and *device_type* parameters are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: include_hierarchy
parameters.description: Specifies whether to retrieve a list of Fireboxes from the linked Subscriber accounts of a Service Provider account. Applicable only if the specified *accountid* is a Service Provider account. The *device* and *include_hierarchy* parameters are mutually exclusive. Allowed values are: true false. Default: false.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Specifies the device ID you want to get the details for. For, Access Points and FireClusters you must specify the `AP-` and `FBCL-` prefixes respectively. For example, `AP-12345`, `FBCL-266366`. For Fireboxes, the `FB-` prefix is optional. For example,`59432` or `FB-59432`. The *device* parameter cannot be combined with *include_hierarchy* or *device_type*.

200.description: Returns a list of devices for the account. When the *device* query parameter is set, the response returns the details of the specified device with a `count` of 1.

list_with_hierarchy.summary: Service Provider account list that includes Subscriber account devices.

detail.summary: Single device detail when the *device* query parameter is specified.

accountid.name: accountid
accountid.description: Specifies the WatchGuard Cloud account ID.

device.name: device
device.description: Specifies the Firebox ID in WatchGuard Cloud. For templates api, mutually exclusive with *templateid*. If omitted and *templateid* is also omitted, the request returns templates available to the account.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Maximum number of exceptions to return in the the response.

start_after.name: start_after
start_after.description: ID of the first exception to return in the response. The value must be a valid exception ID.

templateid.name: templateid
templateid.description: Account level Template ID to filter objects. Mutually exclusive with device parameter.For templates api, if omitted and *device* is also omitted, the request returns templates available to the account.

tags.name: Exceptions (Blocked Sites)
tags.description: The Blocked Sites list specifies sites that cannot make a connection through the Firebox. The Firebox does not block traffic from sites you add to the Blocked Sites Exception list.

tags.name: Exceptions (Botnet)
tags.description: Botnet site exceptions specify sites that you do not want to block, even if they are known botnet sites that the Botnet Detection service added to the Blocked SItes list.

tags.name: Exceptions (File)
tags.description: File exceptions identify files that you do not want the Firebox to scan with APT Blocker, Data Loss Prevention, Gateway AntiVirus, and IntelligentAV.

tags.name: Exceptions (Geolocation)
tags.description: Geolocation exceptions identify sites that you do not want the Geolocation service to block.

tags.name: Exceptions (Intrusion Prevention)
tags.description: IPS signature exceptions specify IPS signature IDs that you do not want the Firebox to use to block connections.

tags.name: Exceptions (WebBlocker)
tags.description: WebBlocker exceptions specify that WebBlocker must always allow or always deny access to a website, regardless of the WebBlocker content category.

tags.name: Global Exceptions
tags.description: Before you can deploy the exceptions you configure with the Firebox Management API to a device, you must enable global exceptions on the device.
